defects.quote: **FISH-01** The tank is a square with walls; the ball moves in straight lines at constant speed and bounces off walls.
defects.evidence: Turn 1: "Environment 2: a circular tank with a ball bouncing around inside it". The spec makes the tank a square, and the FISH-01 example ("heading into the right wall ... its sideways direction reverses") is square-wall physics. No later message changes the shape.
defects.fix: FISH-01: "The tank is a circle with a wall; the ball moves in straight lines at constant speed and bounces off the wall (reflected about the wall's normal at the contact point)." Example: "Given the ball touching the wall, when it bounces, then its velocity is reflected about the radius through the contact point and its speed is unchanged." Also update docs/spec.md FISH-03 and FISH-07 ("one quarter of the tank's width" → "of the tank's diameter") and the FISH edge case ("slides along it" → along the circular wall). In docs/packages/rllab/tests.md TC-08, replace "its normal component flips at each wall touch" with the reflection about the radius, and write "¼ tank diameter".

defects.quote: **FISH-04** An episode lasts 1,000 steps; the score is hits per fish per episode (lower is better).
defects.evidence: Turn 1: fish "must learn to swim away from the ball and survive as long as possible". The developer's goal is survival time. The spec instead respawns a hit fish (FISH-03) and scores hit counts, so 'survive as long as possible' is never measured.
defects.fix: Make the score survival: a fish touched by the ball leaves the episode (as a caught prey does). The episode ends at 1,000 steps or when every fish is hit. Score = mean steps survived per fish (higher is better). Rewrite FISH-03 to match (no respawn), and update the FISH-04 example, FISH-09/FISH-10 wording, docs/packages/rllab/tests.md TC-07 (oracle and direction `higher`) and TC-25 ("every run above the rule mean"), and LOG-05's example "hits per fish". If the developer prefers hit counting, they must say so in their own words.

defects.quote: **PREY-01** The arena is a square with walls, 6 prey, 2 predators and 10 food pellets
defects.evidence: Turn 1: "prey fish forage for food pellets while a learning predator hunts them". The developer named a single predator; the spec has 2.
defects.fix: PREY-01: "6 prey, 1 predator and 10 food pellets", example counts "6, 1 and 10". Update docs/packages/rllab/contract.md core.TeamSpec Cases ("predator (1)"), docs/packages/rllab/tests.md TC-09 ("1 predator"), and PREY-06 ("nearest 2 predators" → "the predator"). Alternatively record the developer's explicit agreement to 2 predators.

defects.quote: **QR-02** A batch of 5 runs of one world and variant finishes within 90 minutes on the same laptop, running in parallel.
defects.evidence: Turn 2: "MacBook Pro Apple Silicon CPU only, under ~1 hour training per env". QR-02 allows 90 minutes per variant, and fish has 3 variants, so up to 4.5 hours per env. The turn-6 'Approved' is an approval, not an override of the stated budget.
defects.fix: QR-02: "A batch of 5 runs of one world and variant finishes within 60 minutes on the same laptop, running in parallel." Update the spec Assumption to "one batch of 5 parallel runs ≤ 60 minutes" and docs/packages/rllab/tests.md TC-24 Expected ("the batch ≤ 60 minutes"). Note in the Assumptions that a multi-variant world (fish) gets about an hour per variant unless the developer confirms otherwise.

defects.quote: **Outline:** Fish in all three variants train with PPO, are watched with the sight overlay, and beat both baselines, while snake results reproduce unchanged.

defects.quote: **Expected:** at most 1 of the 20 seeds rejects either null
defects.evidence: Under the null with family-wise α = 0.05 per seed, the number of rejecting seeds out of 20 is about Binomial(20, 0.05). P(≥ 2) = 1 − 0.95^20 − 20·0.05·0.95^19 ≈ 0.26, so a correct implementation fails this oracle about one time in four. The case's own note ("about 1 in 20 seeds may reject by chance") is the expected value, not a bound.
defects.fix: Expected: "at most 4 of the 20 seeds reject either null" (P(X ≥ 5) ≈ 0.003 for Binomial(20, 0.05)). Tolerance: "binomial bound at 0.5% for a correct family-wise α of 0.05".

defects.evidence: In predator-prey, in-training evaluation plays each team against the co-trained opponent (TC-33: diagonal cell "pairs the prey and predator checkpoints saved at the same step, played on the same 20 seeds as that step's in-training evaluation"). BaselineMeans are measured "in predator-prey each team's baselines play the rule-based opponent". Collapse and the learning-curve baseline lines therefore compare scores taken against different opponents, so neither measures what LOG-03/PREY edge case say.
defects.fix: In train.run_train Invariants, state the in-training opponent: "in multi-team worlds each team is also evaluated against the rule-based opponent at every 5% (EvalPoint.scores_vs_rule)". Use those scores for `collapse` and for the curve's baseline comparison, and keep the co-trained scores for PREY-10's two-team curve. Alternatively compute BaselineMeans against the co-trained opponent and say so in baselines.BaselineMeans.
